strings.name: Wizkid
strings.summary: Born Ayodeji Ibrahim Balogun, Wizkid developed in Lagos church and studio settings. Superstar established his Nigerian profile, while collaborations with Drake, Beyoncé and Tems widened his international audience. Made in Lagos joined light melodies, R&B and African pop rhythms. He continued with Morayo and a joint EP with Asake.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Expanded global audiences through African pop and international collaborations, becoming an important representative of Nigerian Afrobeats abroad.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Sang in church as a child, began recording around eleven and learned songwriting in local studios.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Lagos to international audiences
strings.highlights.h1.text: Collaborations including One Dance brought Nigerian pop to wider markets.
strings.highlights.h2.title: The reach of Essence
strings.highlights.h2.text: The Made in Lagos collaboration with Tems widened Afrobeats' international radio audience.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Released a joint EP
strings.timeline.t1.text: Released REAL, Vol. 1 with Asake, continuing to combine Afrobeats and local musical forms.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Released Morayo
strings.timeline.t2.text: Dedicated the album to his mother, continuing work through Starboy and international labels.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Shared a Grammy
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won best music video as a collaborator on Brown Skin Girl.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Released Made in Lagos
strings.timeline.t4.text: The album included Essence with Tems and subsequently gained wider international reach.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Released Sounds from the Other Side
strings.timeline.t5.text: Worked with RCA on an album extending his mixture of dancehall, pop and African rhythms.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Collaborated on One Dance
strings.timeline.t6.text: The song with Drake and Kyla topped charts in the United States and other countries.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Debut-album breakthrough
strings.timeline.t7.text: Superstar established his profile through songs including Holla at Your Boy.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Signed with E.M.E.
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joined Banky W's Empire Mates Entertainment and entered professional label production.
